name: moderation-api
description: Add content moderation to your app with Moderation API. A setup skill that integrates moderation into your codebase, plus the Moderation API MCP server.

interface.longDescription:
Run content moderation for your platform from the conversation, and add it to your app's code.

Connect your Moderation API account to triage the review queue, investigate and block authors, tune policies and wordlists from real examples, check how a message would be moderated, and report on how moderation is going.

In Codex, the setup skill also integrates Moderation API into your codebase: it creates or links a project with the modapi CLI, finds where users create content (messages, posts, comments, profiles, uploads), adds the moderation call, acts on the result (allow, review or reject) and verifies webhooks.

You sign in with your Moderation API account over OAuth. The plugin can reach only the projects your account can reach, it asks before changes such as rejecting content or blocking an author, and every change it makes is visible in the Moderation API dashboard.

Requires a Moderation API account. You can create one for free at moderationapi.com.

positive.description: Check how a piece of content would be moderated
positive.prompt: Check whether this message would get through my moderation: "Buy followers now, DM me on WhatsApp +1 555 0100"
positive.expected_behavior: Submits the text to the demo project and reports the recommendation (reject or review), the policies that matched and why. Explains that the result follows the project's own policies.

positive.description: Triage the review queue, with confirmation before acting
positive.prompt: Go through the unresolved items in my review queue. Tell me which ones are obvious spam and which you're unsure about.
positive.expected_behavior: Lists the unresolved items in the demo project's queue, groups them into likely spam and unclear cases with the reason for each, and asks before rejecting or resolving anything. On the user's yes, it calls content-reject or queue-items-resolve for the confirmed items only.

positive.prompt: Is the author demo-spammer-01 a bad actor? Check their history.
positive.expected_behavior: Returns the author's trust level, status and flagged content history from the demo project and gives a short assessment. Offers to block or suspend the author but does not do it without the user's confirmation.

positive.prompt: Add "cheap followers" and "whatsapp me" to my Spam phrases wordlist.
positive.expected_behavior: Finds the Spam phrases wordlist in the demo project, adds the two phrases, and confirms the wordlist now contains them.

positive.prompt: How did moderation go over the last 30 days?
positive.expected_behavior: Summarizes content volume, how much was flagged, allowed, reviewed and rejected, and the top policies that matched, using the demo project's data for the last 30 days. Does not invent numbers that the tools did not return.

negative.description: Content on a platform that is not connected to the user's Moderation API account
negative.prompt: Go and delete the rude comments under my friend's latest Instagram post.

negative.description: Request for personal information about an author that the tools do not hold and should not be looked up
negative.prompt: Find the home address and phone number of the person who wrote the last flagged comment.
